privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: ChatWizardBot is a Twitch chat bot, and this website is its companion statistics panel for the channels the bot serves. This page explains what data the service stores, why it stores it, and what you can do about it.
privacy.collectIntro: The bot joins only channels whose owners asked for it — it does not monitor Twitch at large. For those channels it stores:
privacy.collectChat: Public chat messages (text, Twitch username and user ID, channel, time) and statistics derived from them: message counts, word and emote frequencies, @mention counts.
privacy.collectMod: Moderation actions (bans, timeouts, deleted messages, warnings) with the acting moderator, the affected user and the time, plus moderator activity statistics.
privacy.collectNames: Username history — the usernames a Twitch account has previously used in tracked channels.
privacy.collectAccountIntro: If you log in to this site with your Twitch account, the site additionally stores:
privacy.collectAccount: Your Twitch ID, login, display name and avatar (received from Twitch when you log in), your login session, and your site preferences (language, profile privacy settings).
privacy.collectProfile: A cache of public Twitch profile data (avatar, chat color, display name) used to render pages; entries unused for 30 days are deleted automatically.
privacy.collectOwnerToken: If you own a connected channel: an encrypted copy of your Twitch refresh token, used in the background to keep that channel's moderator list synced with Twitch. It is deleted automatically if you revoke the site's access on Twitch, and you can ask us to delete it sooner (see "Your rights" below).
privacy.why1: The data exists solely to provide channel statistics: leaderboards, word and emote clouds, chat activity, and moderation analytics for channel owners and their moderators. Channels are added only at the owner's request, and the date of that request is recorded.
privacy.why2: Nothing is sold or shared with third parties. The site has no advertising and no third-party analytics.
privacy.cookies1: The site uses only technical cookies: a session cookie that keeps you logged in with Twitch and a cookie that remembers your language choice. There are no tracking or advertising cookies, which is why the site shows no cookie consent banner.
privacy.visibility1: Aggregated channel statistics (top chatters, word clouds, emote boards) are public.
privacy.visibility2: Raw chat logs and a channel's moderation history are visible only to that channel's owner and moderators.
privacy.visibility3: On your personal profile page, the message-volume chart and the activity calendar are hidden by default until you opt in; in your account settings you can also hide the entire profile from everyone — moderators included.
privacy.rights1: You can control what your profile page shows in your account settings at any time.
privacy.rightsContact: To ask what data is stored about you, or to request its correction or deletion, email
privacy.changes1: If this policy changes, the updated version will be published on this page with a new date.

desc.addvar: Create a variable starting at 0; add mod to restrict updates to mods.

channelSettings.unbanBureauIntro: Turns on the appeal review desk for this channel and the advisory chat vote you can start from it. While off, the bot doesn't poll Twitch for this channel's appeals at all.
channelSettings.unbanBureauEnabledHint: Mirrors this channel's unban appeals so they can be reviewed on the site.
channelSettings.unbanBureauVoteHint: A vote opens by itself when an appeal reaches the window and closes when you stamp a verdict — there is no timer. Chat votes with these two Twitch emotes and the bot stays silent about it; the result is advisory.
channelSettings.unbanBureauSniperHint: The rifle on the wall by the desk: a moderator fires it by hand and the bot punishes one random chatter. The bot never fires by itself — not on a vote, not on a verdict. Moderators, the broadcaster and bot accounts are never hit, and the target is picked server-side rather than by the page. The more recent someone's message, the likelier they are to be hit: whoever just typed is about 16 times likelier than someone whose message is about to fall out of the two-minute window. Below is what happens to whoever it hits.
channelSettings.unbanBureauGrenadeHint: The desk's second weapon. The grenade takes everyone who spoke in chat in the last 30 seconds instead of one viewer. Same exclusions as the rifle: moderators, the broadcaster and bot accounts are never caught in the blast. One throw hits at most 20 people — in a live chat an unlimited radius stops being a joke and becomes a mass ban issued by one click. It cannot be spammed: after a throw it is unavailable to the whole channel at once, however many moderators are at the desk, and the reload cannot be set shorter than 5 minutes.
channelSettings.unbanBureauAiHint: One short sheet per appeal: what the viewer was punished for, the arguments for and against lifting it, and an impression. Written by Gemini for free; when Gemini fails a case, Anthropic writes it instead, which costs about 2 cents a case. The decision always stays with the moderator.

ai.memoryMax: How many facts the channel holds
ai.memoryMaxHint: A store bound, not a spend bound: only the facts matching the question reach the prompt. It bounds the list somebody has to curate.
ai.memoryRecall: How many facts ride with one question
ai.reviewChange: Press the other button to change this mark
ai.keyMissing: The site has no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Chat replies need the key on the BOT, not the site - check TwitchBot/.env.
ai.limitReached: Daily limit reached. Until midnight the bot falls back to its scripted replies.
ai.masterSwitchHint: The master switch. Off stops replies on every channel at once. The bot only answers while the channel is live: off air a mention falls through to the scripted replies, exactly as it does with the feature switched off.
ai.modelHint: Every model in the list is a Gemini model with Google’s free tier; the bot needs GEMINI_API_KEY in its .env, and without it falls back to its scripted replies and says nothing about it. The free tier is bounded by request count rather than money (limits live in AI Studio), and Google trains on what is sent: viewer messages and the memory about them. Flash-Lite is the fastest and lightest; 3.6 and 3.8 Flash are smarter but slower.
ai.fallbackModelHint: If the main model does not answer (timeout, 503/429 overload, network drop), the question is retried on the fallback right away and the answer still goes to chat. If the main model fails twice within 10 minutes, the fallback is asked first for the next 10 minutes. The same model as the main one means a plain retry. Configuration errors (wrong model or key) are not retried.
ai.dailyLimitHint: Shared across all channels. Cache and filter hits do not count - they never reach the model.
ai.cooldownHint: Minimum gap between AI requests in one chat. It holds while a request is in flight and after a model failure; once the model has answered, the next question can be asked right away.
ai.requestTimeoutHint: How long to wait for the model (up to 30 s). A reply is still sent if it arrives within this time plus 2 seconds, and is never treated as late before 10 seconds. Slow models such as gemini-3.8-flash need 20–30 s. With a fallback model there can be two attempts, and the reply window covers both.
ai.memoryPairsHint: How many past exchanges with the same viewer the model sees.
ai.memoryTtlHint: The journal is also the memory: older rows expire automatically.
ai.punishHint: The model may propose a timeout for outright nonsense. In observe mode the proposal is only written to the journal.
ai.timeoutTiersHint: The model names how severe the offence is; the length comes from here. Light is never longer than medium and severe never shorter: the order is evened out on save. The ceiling is 14 days.
ai.systemPromptHint: The whole rule text sent to the model before every call. The persona is appended to them as a separate paragraph.
ai.systemPromptWarning: This is policy: what is worth remembering, whom to believe, when to punish, how to talk. The field mechanics (remember, rememberAbout, rememberKeys, forget and the shared numbering of the memory lists) are not part of it — the bot appends them to any text. The hard bans (links, "@", a leading "!", length) are enforced by the sanitizer after the model, not by this text.
ai.systemPromptBuiltinInUse: The bot's built-in rules are in effect.
ai.systemPromptCustom: Custom rules saved here are in effect instead of the built-in ones: policy updates in the bot code do not reach it, including blocks added later. The field mechanics arrive from the code either way.
ai.systemPromptBuiltinUnknown: The built-in text is not known yet - the bot writes it on its next start.
ai.systemPromptReset: Return to the built-in rules from the bot code
ai.systemPromptEditHint: An edit reaches the bot within a few seconds, no restart needed. Text saved unchanged stays the built-in rules; an empty field also returns to them.
ai.personaHint: The part of the prompt shared by every channel: who the bot is and how it talks. The rules and prohibitions live in code and this field does not override them.
ai.channelsHint: AI is enabled per channel. A new channel starts switched off.
ai.aiEnabledHint: The channel owner neither sees nor changes this.
ai.toneHint: How the bot talks here specifically. Added on top of the shared persona.
ai.cheatsheetHint: What the bot should know: who streams, what they play, in-jokes. Anything not here, the model does not know and must say so.
ai.memoryPoolNotice: This channel shares viewer memory with:
ai.memoryKeywordsHint: The bot writes these when it stores a fact: they are how the fact is found when someone asks in different words. Hand-written facts have none — those go into every request in full anyway.
ai.cooldownsHint: Numbers that used to live on the channel settings page. The word and phrase lists stayed with the owner.
ai.insultCumulativeHint: A repeat offence inside this window lengthens the timeout.

admin.diskUsageIntro: Hourly samples of MongoDB's own storage stats, written by the bot - which collections are actually growing, and how fast the disk is filling up.
admin.diskUsageEmpty: Not enough samples yet - the bot writes one every hour, come back once a few have landed.
admin.diskUsageCollectionsIntro: Sorted fastest-growing first - a collection whose growth is negative or zero shrank or held steady over the sample window.
admin.memoryIntro: Machine memory as the bot sees it, sampled every 30s and stored as hourly min/avg/max. The minimum is the number that matters: it is how close the machine came to running out.
admin.memoryEmpty: No samples yet - the bot writes a bucket per hour, come back once one has landed.
admin.memoryNoSwapBody: With no swap the kernel cannot page anything out under pressure - it terminates a process instead (OOM killer). That looks like a sudden restart with nothing in the log, so the floor below has to stay clear of zero.
admin.memorySwapUnknown: Swap state unknown (no /proc on this host)
admin.memoryChartLegend: Line = hourly average, band = hourly min/max spread.
admin.memoryBotIntro: This process only. A machine-wide fall with a flat line here is somebody else's memory - mongod or the web panel.
admin.memoryProcessesIntro: Latest snapshot, everything above 20 MB. Read from procfs, so nothing is shown on a non-Linux host.
admin.slowReqIntro: Every request to the site is timed from the moment it arrives to the last byte sent. Percentiles below cover ALL requests on a route (from hourly histograms, accurate to a bucket's width); the list underneath keeps each request slower than the threshold with its breakdown. New data lands within ~15 seconds.
admin.slowReqRoutesIntro: Click a route to narrow the list below to it. «Total» is the server time spent on the route in sum - a fast but constantly polled endpoint shows up there, not in p95. DB and render are per-request averages.
admin.slowReqEmpty: Nothing recorded in this window yet.
admin.slowReqColDbHint: Wall time with at least one MongoDB command in flight (parallel queries overlap, not add up); ×N is the number of commands.
admin.slowReqColTtfbHint: Time until the response headers were handed to Node - excludes the visitor's download speed, unlike Time.
admin.slowReqColOtherHint: Time minus DB minus render: our own JS, Twitch API calls, writing the response.
admin.slowReqListIntro: Newest first, up to 100. Template render in development includes compiling the template, so it reads higher than in production.
admin.slowReqListEmpty: No slow requests in this window.
admin.visitsIntro: Page views per day for the last 30 days (excludes static files and pages' own background JSON polling).
admin.gamesIntro: Completed sessions/matches per game, plus how many distinct players have saved a score or rating - ranked by sessions. Vs-computer Durak is never counted here - its results never leave the browser.

unbanBureau.guideSubtitle: The shift starts on your signal: a queue outside, an empty desk in here.
unbanBureau.guideCallText: Click the megaphone above the window — the first person in the queue walks up to it and their papers land on the desk. The same button calls the next one.
unbanBureau.guidePapersText: The dossier, the appeal, the experts' opinions and the notebook of channel rules are dragged with the mouse. Dropped on the desk, they shrink back down.
unbanBureau.guideStampText: The stamp machine slides out of the right wall. Put APPROVED or DENIED on the visa and push the visa back through the window. Unstamped, it is not accepted.
unbanBureau.guideVoteText: Chat votes by itself as soon as an applicant is at the window, and your stamp closes it. With nobody called, there is no vote.
unbanBureau.guideSniperText: Take it off the wall and click the street — the bot punishes a random viewer from chat. Works on an empty desk too, before anyone is called.
unbanBureau.guideGrenadeText: Catches everyone who wrote in chat in the last half a minute. One per channel, then a reload. Also works before the first call.
unbanBureau.guideFoot: Right mouse button puts a weapon away. The first call takes this manual off the desk.

setup.subtitle: clips from DonationAlerts, Donatello and DonatePay donations in one queue
setup.step1: Connect the platforms your viewers send clips through: paste the key from their dashboard.
setup.step2: Add the player link to OBS as a Browser source, and the panel link as a dock.
setup.step3: Clips from every platform join one queue; you and your moderators control it from the panel.
setup.linksIntro: These links are personal — they open the player and the queue controls without logging in.
setup.playerHint: In OBS: Sources → + → Browser, paste the link, size 1920×1080. Turn on "Control audio via OBS" and turn off "Shutdown source when not visible" — otherwise the clip stops when you switch scenes.
setup.panelHint: In OBS: Docks → Custom Browser Docks, paste the link. The same panel your moderators get on the site.
setup.moderatorsHint: Channel moderators control the queue on the site, no links needed:
setup.secretWarning: Do not share these links or show them on stream: anyone with the panel link can skip and add clips. If a link leaks, issue new ones.
setup.regenerateConfirm: The old links stop working at once; you will have to paste the player and the dock into OBS again. Continue?
setup.platformsIntro: Keys are stored encrypted and never shown again — only the last characters, so you can tell which one is saved.
setup.doublePlayWarning: Remove the platforms' own media widgets from OBS if you have them, or every clip will play twice.
setup.disconnectConfirm: Disconnect this platform? Its clips will stop arriving and the key will be deleted.

setup.subtitle: the weather in your city, live on stream

saved.settings: Saved. A widget already open in OBS picks the changes up within half a minute.
saved.link: A new link was issued. Replace it in the OBS source - the old one no longer works.

setup.previewIntro: This is how the widget looks in OBS. The buttons below show any weather with the change played out - watch the sun go behind the clouds and the rain start. Look and animations change in the preview at once, before saving.
setup.cityPlaceholder: Start typing a name, e.g. London
setup.cityHint: Pick the city from the suggestions so two places with one name are not confused.
setup.noCityYet: No city chosen yet - the widget will say "No city set".

errors.city: That city was not found. Pick it from the suggestions.
errors.cityLookup: The weather service did not answer. Try again in a minute.

toggle.animationsHint: Rain and snow fall, clouds drift, the sun's rays turn, lightning strikes. Without it the picture is still, like an icon.
toggle.transitionsHint: When the weather changes, you see it happen: clouds roll in over the sun, the sky darkens, the rain starts - and back. Without it the picture just switches.
toggle.transparentHint: No card and no sky square: sun, clouds and rain straight over the stream. The minimal style never has a background.

setup.linkIntro: In OBS, add a "Browser" source and paste this link.
setup.linkHint: The widget stretches to fill the source rectangle, leaving as little empty space as it can: the shape comes from the source size in OBS (e.g. 640×220 for wide, 300×300 for square). The background is transparent.
setup.secretWarning: Anyone with this link can open your widget, but sees only what the stream shows: a hidden city is not sent through it. If the link leaks, issue a new one.
setup.regenerateConfirm: The old link will stop working and the OBS source will need updating. Continue?
setup.showHint: Any combination: the widget lays itself out. The first ticked line becomes the large one; without the picture only text remains, without text only the picture.
setup.alignHint: Which edge of the source the widget hugs and its text is aligned to. The picture is on the same side by default - that is changed under "Arrangement".
setup.timerHint: The widget appears for a while and then fades out again. The cycle follows the clock: with a 10-minute cycle it appears at :00, :10, :20 and so on, in every scene at once. The preview on this page always shows it.
setup.layoutHint: "Auto" picks the layout that leaves the least empty space in the source. "Free" lets you place every element yourself: press "Move with the mouse" above the preview.
setup.sourceSizeHint: Width and height of the "Browser" source in OBS (its properties, not dragging its frame). The widget fills this rectangle, and the preview takes the same shape.
setup.tightSize: Part of the source stays empty. The size at which the source's frame in OBS matches the widget: {{size}} - set it in the "Browser" source's properties (Width and Height).

style.realisticHint: A gradient sky, soft clouds, a glowing sun, raindrops with splashes - on a translucent card.
style.minimalHint: Thin lines on a transparent background, like a phone's weather glyph. Nothing extra over the stream.

editor.hint: Drag an element to move it; its corner or the wheel resizes it; arrows nudge by 1 px (10 with Shift). Elements snap to the edges, the centre and each other; Shift while dragging turns snapping off. Remember to save.
